stem:
Omkar must construct rectangle $ABCD$ so that diagonal $AC$ divides $\angle DAB$ into $60^\circ$ and $30^\circ$.

Which plan locates the next sides and vertex $D$ correctly?

options.text: Call the finished figure diagonal $AC$ only, without using the right angle at $A$ or the $60^\circ$ and $30^\circ$ parts.
Say that drawing diagonal $AC$ is what creates rectangle $ABCD$, instead of building the rectangle from right angles and equal opposite sides.
Use $\angle DAB=90^\circ$, so the $60^\circ$ part leaves $30^\circ$; then place $D$ with right angles (or equal opposite sides) from the known sides.
Choose the plan only because $60$ is the largest printed angle number among $60$ and $30$.

teacher.key_rationale: In a rectangle every corner is $90^\circ$, so a diagonal that cuts one corner into $60^\circ$ leaves $30^\circ$; vertex $D$ follows from right angles or equal opposite sides. Relabeling as the diagonal alone, reversing diagonal and rectangle, or grabbing the printed $60$ all miss that construction.
